labels.notes: No assertion of theo:CBG (ETT.tex:1884-1887: a maximal Cauchy extension exists and is unique) is proved or claimed. The module cites the label unmarked (l.6, with ETT.tex:1884, correct) as the consumer of A2's last field. grep finds no bold-backtick form anywhere in the file. The quotes at l.16-18 and l.20-24 are verbatim ETT.tex:1885-1886 and 2346-2350. The REPORT's 'partial', marked false, matches the ledger row (LEDGER.md:891, partial) and the precedent of T-ett-diamant-past. (1) THE CONCLUSION. #check gives SingularRowsSecondCountable.secondCountable_of_cauchy : {M : Type u_1} [TopologicalSpace M] [SingularGXStructure (Flat.isom 2) (Minkowski 2) M] {C : Causality M} [T2Space M] [ConnectedSpace M], IsoChartsCoverDEC25 ... -> C.GloballyHyperbolic -> forall S : Set M, C.IsCauchySurface S -> SecondCountableTopology S -> SecondCountableTopology M. The field CBG.Geometry.secondCountable_of_cauchy (Causal/CBG/Geometry.lean:339-341) is: forall {M} [TopologicalSpace M] [T2Space M] [ConnectedSpace M] (s : Str M), (causality s).GloballyHyperbolic -> forall S, (causality s).IsCauchySurface S -> SecondCountableTopology S -> SecondCountableTopology M. So the conclusion is the field's word for word, with C for causality s, and IsCauchySurface is the same DEC-14 predicate (Causal/Cauchy.lean:67-73). LocalModel's field (:625-628) has the same conclusion over a ChartedSpace Y M. The SCOPE says truthfully that it is not instantiated here. The structure is read as [SingularGXStructure] plus hC. The earlier A2 rows read it as hmin plus hC (SingularRowsDiamondPast.isCompact_Jminus_inter_Jplus, l.251-254), so this reading is weaker: no AbsolutelyMinimal. The natural form takes MassACovered plus IsAtlasCausalityDEC25, exactly as SingularRowsDiamondPast's _of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 (l.280-283). NO COUNTABILITY OF M SNEAKS IN. No M-level statement has a SecondCountableTopology M binder (#check of all of them). SingularGXStructure (Causal/Port/SingularAtlas.lean:1539-1543) carries only the atlas and its maximality. In the file's own variable context plus [T2Space M] [ConnectedSpace M] and hC, '#synth SecondCountableTopology M' fails. Since the theorem typechecks without that instance and with standard axioms, no used lemma can have consumed it. The only SecondCountableTopology instances in play are proved ones: Reg M (haveI from secondCountableTopology_reg, l.345), the chart sources U i (l.355) and the models (l.114-119). [ConnectedSpace M] is really used: IsPortly.isConnected (Portly.lean:219) needs it. (2) THE COUNTABILITY ARGUMENT is sound, and the proof of countable_sing_inter (l.249-278) is the textbook one. D = Sing M seen in S. For d in D, exists_isOpen_inter_sing_subset gives an open W containing d with W meeting Sing M inside the component K of sing_alpha through d. Any y in D with y in W lies in K and in S. existsUnique_mem_component_inter then forces y = d, so {d} = D minus the preimage of W, and D is discrete. D is second countable as a subspace of S, hence separable, hence countable (separableSpace_iff_countable). The openness of K in Sing M is V and W together. V is the open set with sing_alpha = V meeting Sing (SFALocal.exists_isOpen_sing_eq_inter, SFALocal.lean:317). W is local_onto of the line development at t = 0. At BTZ points (alpha = 0) the development is SFALine.exists_isLineDevelopment (SFALine.lean:252). At massive points (alpha > 0, alpha != 2 pi) it is LineDevelopment.exists_development with SFAMassiveLine.isTranslationAtlas (SFAMassiveLine.lean:159). alpha = 2 pi is empty by SFALocal.sing_two_pi (:386), since the cone of angle 2 pi is regular. Uniqueness on S is DEC-14 applied to the inextensible curve over univ from SFALine.line (alpha = 0) or SFAMassiveLine.massive_line (alpha > 0), whose range is K. Both signatures ask only [T2Space M] and hC. The components of sing_alpha are the components of Sing M: each sing_alpha is relatively open in Sing M and they are pairwise disjoint (SFALocal.disjoint_sing), so each is also relatively closed. The REPORT's wording 'each component of Sing(M)' is therefore correct. (3) WITNESSES. All three get their conclusions from the M-level theorems (kb/0011): secondCountableTopology_of_isCauchySurface (nonvacuous_e0, nonvacuous_sublevel) and secondCountable_of_cauchy_of_isAtlasCausalityDEC25 (nonvacuous_e0_natural). Each shows the hypotheses met with a BTZ point on S. They are vacuous in spirit as to the conclusion. E0 is second countable by instance (TopologicalSpace.instSecondCountableTopologyProd), {T < 1} by the subspace instance, and hSc is inferInstance through that instance (l.403, 428, 463). The file's SCOPE (l.92-95) and the REPORT notes disclose this. The curation must say it on the row, as wave 31 did for its identity witnesses: 'the witnesses are E0 and {T < 1}, both already second countable by instance; they show the hypotheses satisfiable with a BTZ point on S, not the conclusion new'. CHEAP WITNESS WITHOUT AN SC INSTANCE: none. The only singular (Isom, Minkowski) structures in lean-causal are E0 (E0GX.singularGX), E_alpha (EAlphaGX.singularGX), MassAModel o, and open subsets of them (opensSingularGXStructure). Each is a subspace of a second countable product, so its second countability is an instance. grep finds no quotient or glued singular manifold. Such a witness would need new infrastructure (a quotient of E0, or the CBG gluing at E0), which is not cheap. (4) FINDING (rem:CBG_manquant (i)). It is a suggestion, not a claimed error, and it is true. The Lean theorem shows that a Hausdorff, connected E>=0-manifold (DEC-25) with a second countable Cauchy surface is second countable, with no global hyperbolicity and no Geroch argument on the singular part. Hausdorffness is used. See minor finding 2 for the inputs its application to the limit leaves implicit.

findings.what: The general clause is accurate: Hausdorff, connected, E>=0 (DEC-25), a second countable Cauchy surface. For the limit, the finding names only Hausdorffness and 'S is the image of Sigma_0'. It leaves out two inputs the theorem also needs: connectedness of the limit (immediate, as a directed union of connected extensions all containing the image of M0), and the second countability of that image in the limit's subspace topology (it is homeomorphic to Sigma_0 through the open Cauchy embedding, and Sigma_0 is a subspace of the second countable M0). The remark itself mentions only Hausdorffness and the structure.
findings.fix: When curating rem:CBG_manquant's paper_findings, write: '... applies to the limit, which is Hausdorff, connected, and has the second countable Cauchy surface phi(Sigma_0)'.

findings.what: Every witness has only a BTZ point on S, so the massive branch (alpha > 0: exists_development with SFAMassiveLine.isTranslationAtlas, massive_line) is never run on a concrete manifold. A massive witness is cheap. SFALocal.nonvacuous_epi gives hC at E_pi and a non-empty sing pi. SingularRowsGeroch.nonvacuous_epi_geroch gives connectedness and a Cauchy surface. S is second countable by instance. existsUnique_mem_component_inter would put a massive point on S. kb/0011 does not require this, since E0 already meets every hypothesis. It would show the alpha > 0 case of the discreteness argument at work. E_pi is also second countable by instance, which would need disclosing too.
findings.fix: Optional. Add a nonvacuous_epi witness out of secondCountableTopology_of_isCauchySurface at Massive Real.pi, or note in SCOPE that the massive branch has no witness.
